Hi all — looping in technical detail below and answering Anita's numbered points. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

1) Encryption:
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 by default).
- At rest: all customer data stored on disk is AES-256 encrypted. For Hosted customers we use provider-managed KMS by default (AWS KMS / GCP KMS depending on region).
- Customer-managed keys: Supported on Dedicated and Private deployments today. For Hosted we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) roadmap with HSM-backed keys; can provide a timeline and interim compensating controls if BYOK is a hard requirement.

2) PII handling / redaction:
- We do not automatically redact free-text inputs. We recommend pre-send redaction for high-risk fields.
- Options: (a) client-side preprocessing to strip identifiers; (b) use our edge preprocessing hook (runs before inference) to apply regex-based redaction; (c) run in Private where customer controls the preprocessing pipeline.

3) Logging & retention (defaults / config):
- API request logs: default retention 90 days; configurable down to 30 days or up to 365 days depending on plan.
- Inference traces (token-level traces / KV cache logs): default 30 days; can be disabled or extended per environment.
- Audit logs (auth/admin actions): default 12 months for Dedicated/Enterprise; Hosted default 90 days but upgradeable for an additional cost.
- All retention windows are configurable via the Console or via an API for Dedicated/Private.

4) Subprocessors / Telemetrix:
- Telemetrix is used for service-level telemetry (metrics, error rates, aggregated latency histograms). They receive no request bodies or token-level contents in our standard Hosted setup. We send aggregated, sampled metrics.
- If a customer enables advanced debugging support and opts-in to share traces for troubleshooting, traces are redacted by default and require explicit consent (we document this in the support workflow).

5) Marketplace flows:
- Marketplace providers receive billing and usage metering information (account id, usage quantity, timestamps). They do not receive request payloads.
- For sensitive customers, we recommend Dedicated or Private to avoid any marketplace-mediated metadata if that is a blocker.

Attachments: SOC 2 Type II (redacted), updated subprocessor matrix, annotated prod diagram.

If you want a live runbook showing the exact fields sent to Telemetrix or the marketplace, I can produce a short export.

Cheers,

Hi Anita / Samir,

Thanks for the questions. A few legal / contracting points addressing marketplace & subprocessors: 

- Subprocessors: we maintain a subprocessor list and provide 30 days' advance notice before adding new subprocessors. We are open to standard DPA commitments (data processing purposes + subprocessors clause).
- Marketplace: marketplace providers typically act as metering/billing processors and will have access to metadata necessary for billing. If you need to prevent marketplace exposure entirely, the cleanest path is Dedicated or Private where billing can be handled via invoicing rather than marketplace provisioning.
- Telemetry vendors: we classify Telemetrix as a metrics-only subprocessor — not a recipient of request payloads. We can put tighter contractual limits in the subprocessor addendum if required.
- DPA / Redlines: Please send any DPA or clause redlines. We can accept standard UK/US privacy addenda; for HIPAA/BAA-level controls we will need a BAA signature (we have one template we can share).

I’ve attached our SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and an example DPA template. Happy to have our legal ops team schedule a quick redline session.

Regards,
